title: TraceRaysNode keeps its own copy of the tile state machine
body: ComputeDispatchNode and ComputeStageNode now size their submissions through Core/TiledDispatch (lane fable-gpusubmit1). TraceRaysNode still carries the same state machine (tile command buffers, timestamp queries, GpuChunkCost, batches) with pixels as the unit and a ray-tracing stage flag. Move it onto TiledDispatch so the rule has one implementation. Tier luna: mechanical, the helper exists, needs a device with hardware ray tracing to witness.

title: The march launches as one dispatch from a cost persisted in another scene
body: ComputeDispatchNode seeds its tile rule from calibration/ beside the executable, keyed by extent only. After a cheap 1080p run, the RTL scene launches the march as one dispatch for four frames: 531 to 607 ms a submission with the base binary b36758837 (fable-gpusubmit1 run before-rtl-1080), over the 500 ms submit guard. Application.LookdevCapture.GlyphSdf.RtlProof.SubmitGuard therefore depends on which 1080p test last ran from the same build directory. Options and a recommendation are in reports/fable-gpusubmit1.md STOP 1 (launch at the floor until this run has measured the pass). Tier sol: changes the march start-up timing that cl-lookdevfast2 tuned, needs native and Dozen measurement.

title: Native codegen golden check fails with ENOMEM reading sources over the cross-mount
body: fable-gpusubmit1:native-build-2 failed one step, codegen/checks/channel_vocabulary_check.stamp: the WSL dotnet CodegenTool.dll threw System.IO.IOException: Cannot allocate memory while reading /mnt/c/Users/liory/AppData/Local/VIXEN/kernel-codegen/sources/yeroket-<sha>/.../Runtime/Channels/VoxelLayout. Every product target had linked; the identical rerun (native-build-3) passed. The check should read its sources from the Linux side or retry a transient mount error, and say which it was. Tier luna: one check wrapper, needs a repro under memory pressure.

title: The march never learns its launch latency when it refines downward
body: In the RTL scene at 1080p (fable-gpusubmit1 run final-rtl-1080, native Release on ws, device shared) the march costs 339 to 349 ms as one dispatch and 1147 to 1157 ms as 180 tiles. It refines downward from the persisted one-dispatch launch, and GpuChunkCost::ObserveScale replaces its only measured scale with the smaller one, so LaunchLatencyNs stays 0 and the 2 ms budget is never raised. The same defect cost shadow_visibility_wave 495 ms against 228 ms and was fixed for stages in 3a9faa8c5 (ObserveScale keepLarger, TiledDispatch::RefinedTileGroups). Enabling it for Prior::Heaviest changes the march timing on every heavy scene, so it needs a native benchmark witness and a Dozen check. Tier sol: hidden perf behind tuned march behaviour.
